A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EvaGaussians and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A-C. The substantial revisions and renumbering can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and DAVIS experiments on novel-view synthesis and deblurring, including loss ablations and per-scene appendix results.

after.justification: v2 reports revised reconstruction results, expanded loss ablations, and new pose-accuracy and motion-blur robustness experiments, alongside retained empirical results.

M1.justification: v2 Section 3.4 adds event-derived grayscale reconstruction at sampled interframe times and intensity-aware depth regularization. These expand the training objective from two losses to four, substantially changing optimization while retaining EDI initialization and joint camera-pose optimization.

E1.justification: Both retain the synthetic large-scale, medium-scale, and object scenes and five DAVIS scenes for deblurring and novel-view synthesis. v2 additionally evaluates deliberately varied motion-blur conditions in Section 4.6 and Appendix B.3, extending input-condition coverage within the existing datasets.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark tables retain B-NeRF, B-3DGS, UFP-GS, EDI-GS, EFN-GS, E2NeRF, BAD-NeRF, BAD-GS, and EDNeRF. v2 corrects their textual grouping and adds a UFP citation, but introduces no new competing reconstruction method. Initial-versus-optimized poses constitute an additional ablation control.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce ATE comparisons between initial and optimized poses, FPS reporting in Figure 1, and controlled half/default/double camera-speed conditions for blur robustness. The principal image-quality metrics and stated benchmark splits remain unchanged. The newly documented progressive rendering schedule does not establish what resolution schedule v1 actually used.

E4.justification: v2 Table 2 expands the two-loss analysis to four losses across large-scale, medium-scale, and real scenes. Tables 3, 4, and 12 and Figure 7 add pose-accuracy and blur-robustness analyses. The pose-count experiment is retained, while v1's no-loss ablation row and qualitative loss-ablation figure are removed.

E5.justification: v2 Tables 3 and 12 newly report ATE with plus/minus quantities. Their statistical meaning and whether they summarize scenes or repeated runs are unspecified; no seed or repeated-run count is supplied. This establishes changed uncertainty reporting, not an increase in experimental runs.

E6.justification: For the revised model, reported large/medium/object NVS PSNR changes from 25.71/29.94/29.75 to 26.02/30.47/30.24; object PSNR now exceeds EDNeRF's retained 29.83. v2 also updates per-scene NVS scores and adds ATE, blur-severity, and FPS results. Appendix DVS scores remain unchanged. Some updated real-world summaries conflict with v2's other tables, limiting interpretation of those results.

T1.justification: v2 adds mathematical definitions for intensity reconstruction and intensity-weighted depth regularization and expands the total objective in Equations 7-9. The EDI derivation and calibration equations remain equivalent, while v1's explicit Gaussian/covariance preliminaries are removed. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 drops v1's 'first framework' priority claim and adds an explicit claim that event-assisted regularization stabilizes geometry. The central contributions of reconstructing sharp Gaussian scenes, enabling real-time novel views, and providing two datasets remain.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a mechanism linking sparse blurry supervision to floaters and geometry errors, and interprets its new tests as evidence of pose accuracy and blur robustness. It removes v1's specific caveats about sparse objects, reflective or transparent materials, and sky regions from Appendix B and figure captions. The general limitation concerning intricate textures under severe blur remains.

D1.justification: v2 supplies new loss weights, beta=2, 5-by-5 Sobel kernels, and a progressive rendering schedule starting at 0.3 resolution for the first 30% of iterations. It omits v1's explicit 1,000-iteration initialization detail and focal-length file pointer. The project-page destination changes and videos are advertised, while code and dataset release remain promised.

R1.justification: The general event-camera applications survey is replaced by a focused discussion of event-based 3D reconstruction. v2 adds positioning against Ev-NeRF, Robust e-NeRF, Deblur e-NeRF, E-NeRF, and concurrent event-based Gaussian methods, plus references supporting depth regularization. This substantially changes the research context rather than merely updating bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, and appendix discussion. It reorganizes the method into initialization, bundle adjustment, and geometry regularization, moves implementation details into Experiments, and consolidates appendix subsections. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, adds an opening comparison figure, redraws the method diagram, merges four principal benchmark tables, and reorganizes qualitative comparisons. It adds pose-analysis displays and expands the loss-ablation table. Many appendix illustrations are retained or relocated rather than newly generated evidence.

improvement.justification: The new regularization components and diagnostic experiments provide useful substance, but reporting consistency and qualification worsen. v1's real-world summaries agree with its appendix; v2 reports BRISQUE 53.96 in Table 1 versus 56.1472 in Table 11, and MetaIQA .1969 in Table 1 versus .2129 in Tables 2 and 15. Specific failure-case caveats are also removed. These unresolved discrepancies and tradeoffs prevent a reliable net judgment of overall improvement.
